skill.name: ddd-check
skill.description: Checks Java projects for Domain-Driven Design compliance. It supports changed-file reviews and full-project audits for layering, naming, dependencies, and common anti-patterns.

content.value_statement: Java teams can miss layer violations and inconsistent Domain-Driven Design conventions during routine reviews. This skill checks changed files or the full project.
actual_capabilities: Lists changed Java files with git diff for an incremental review.
Discovers production Java files for a full-project audit.
Checks package layers, base classes, naming, imports, and dependency direction.
Flags identity exposure, anemic models, service overuse, and layer coupling.
Reports findings by severity with specific fixes and a concise summary.
limitations: The package does not include the rule and reference files named in its instructions.
Checks rely on model reasoning and text inspection rather than a Java parser.
Incremental mode requires a Git repository with a usable HEAD revision.
Project-specific DDD conventions may differ from the prescribed class names and layers.

use_cases.title: Review a Java change
use_cases.description: Check modified Java files for DDD violations before committing or opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Assess project architecture
use_cases.description: Audit production Java files for layer boundaries, dependency direction, and recurring design problems.

use_cases.title: Standardize team reviews
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent DDD checklist and severity model during code reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Check my changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an incremental DDD check on my changed Java files. Report each violation with its severity and an exact fix.

prompt_templates.title: Review one layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review changed Java files in the {layer} layer. Focus on packages, naming, base classes, imports, and identity protection.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the project
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full DDD audit of this Java project. Summarize layer health, dependency violations, anti-patterns, and prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Java project before a DDD migration. Map violations by layer, identify dependency cycles, and propose a phased remediation order.

output_examples.output: Order.java - Domain - HIGH: Public setId exposes aggregate identity. Make the setter protected and assign identity through aggregate behavior.

output: Executive summary: 42 production files reviewed across five layers.
Critical: Domain code imports an infrastructure mapper.
Priority: Introduce a domain gateway, then move mapping into infrastructure.

output_examples.output: CreateOrderService.java - Application - HIGH: The use case lacks a dedicated executor. Move orchestration into a CreateOrderExecutor.

best_practices: Use incremental mode for routine changes and full mode for planned architecture reviews.
Confirm project-specific base classes and naming rules before accepting findings.
Resolve dependency direction violations before lower-severity style findings.
anti_patterns: Do not treat model findings as a replacement for compilation or automated architecture tests.
Do not run a full audit when the review should remain limited to changed files.
Do not apply prescribed class names without checking the project's established conventions.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets Java projects organized with Domain-Driven Design layers and related naming conventions.

faq.question: What is incremental mode?
faq.answer: Incremental mode uses Git differences from HEAD to review only changed or added Java files.

faq.question: What is full mode?
faq.answer: Full mode discovers production Java files outside target and test directories, then reviews the complete architecture.

faq.question: Does it modify source files?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reads files and reports recommended changes.

faq.question: Does it compile or test the project?
faq.answer: No. It performs a text-based architecture review and does not replace builds, tests, or parser-based checks.

faq.question: Are all referenced rules included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package names rule and reference files that are absent from its file structure.
